teaser.text: Starbucks is a company that sells prepared drinks and food in coffeehouses, and earns money when partners sell branded products. It sells not only ingredients, but also preparation, convenience, choice and a familiar place to sit or move quickly through.

stock.title: Starbucks stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Starbucks stock forecast: the weighted price is $72.08 in October 2027 and $93.20 in October 2029, across bear, base and bull cases.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario is $72.08 in October 2027, before reaching $93.20 in October 2029. It hinges on whether transaction growth—not just a higher ticket—can pay for renewal.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Starbucks works, who its rivals are, how management is executing, and what risks matter.

blocks.heading: Where could Starbucks shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a weak near-term path and only a small three-year gain. The probability-weighted price is $72.08 in October 2027, or a 22% loss including dividends. It is $86.91 in October 2028, a 4% loss, before reaching $93.20 in October 2029, a 5% gain.
The October 2029 outcomes range from $43.43 in the bear case to $168.66 in the bull case, against today’s $95.76.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Starbucks?

paragraphs.text: The bear case earnings are $2,625 million in 2027 and $2,698 million in 2028, reaching $2,772 million in 2029. Revenue rises only from $37,500 million to $38,000 million before reaching $38,500 million. Margins remain near 7.0% and 7.1%, then reach 7.2%. The bull case reaches $3,272 million in 2027 and $4,300 million in 2028, then $5,000 million in 2029. It assumes revenue reaches $43,000 million and margin reaches 11.6%, requiring durable traffic gains and labor productivity. The uneven earnings record and restructuring burden support the wider downside.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Starbucks really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash flow less spending on property and equipment. In fiscal 2025, Starbucks generated $4,747.5 million of operating cash and spent $2,305.5 million on property and equipment. Calculated free cash flow was therefore $2,442.0 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Starbucks today?

paragraphs.text: The forward P/E measures the price against estimated earnings per share. The current multiple implies about $3.15 of earnings over the next twelve months, but that estimate can be distorted by repurchases, restructuring and the one-time $536.3 million China divestiture gain.

blocks.heading: How much does Starbucks pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The dividend is a stabilizer, not the investment case. The latest quarterly rate is $0.63, annualized at $2.52. The base case moves from $2.52 to $2.60 and then $2.68; the bear case holds at $2.52; the bull case reaches $2.96. The pause is credible because FY2025 dividends exceeded calculated free cash flow, although the latest increase and long record make a cut less likely.

blocks.heading: Is Starbucks’ dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash flow less spending on property and equipment. In fiscal 2025, Starbucks generated $4,747.5 million of operating cash and spent $2,305.5 million on property and equipment. Calculated free cash flow was therefore $2,442.0 million.

Starbucks paid $2,771.4 million in dividends in 2025, more than calculated free cash flow. That does not prove the dividend is unsafe, but it makes maintenance spending, future cash generation and the balance sheet central questions.

The forecast moves toward the bear case if FY2027 and FY2028 results show stalled transactions, worsening waits or accuracy, rising labor cost per transaction, and weaker operating margins. Persistent closure and turnaround spending would further reduce cash available for buybacks.

blocks.heading: What is Starbucks’ dividend yield at its share price?

paragraphs.text: At today’s price, Starbucks is valued for a recovery in lasting profits, not for a generous cash yield.

blocks.heading: What has Starbucks guided for fiscal 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management raised its full-year adjusted earnings forecast on July 29. “Adjusted” earnings remove specified items from standard accounting, so they aim to show the underlying business more clearly, though the excluded costs may still require cash. The guidance table brings together sales growth, revenue, margin, earnings, openings and restructuring costs.

blocks.heading: What has Starbucks’ revenue and profit trend been over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Operating margin fell to 7.9% in fiscal 2025 from 15.0% in 2024. Restructuring and impairment charges reduced current profit, while a litigation benefit increased it. Removing specified charges, transaction costs and the benefit produces a 9.9% adjusted operating margin, still well below the previous year.
June 2026 showed better customer demand, but the profit jump overstated the improvement in ordinary earnings.

blocks.heading: What should Starbucks watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: Starbucks plans to report its fourth-quarter and full-year results after the market closes on October 29, 2026. The report should show whether the September sales target held and how the late closure plan affected earnings. The reconciliation will matter because adjusted profit can exclude restructuring costs even when related payments reduce cash.

North America offers the clearest operating test. Transactions show whether customers are returning; margin shows whether Starbucks earns more after paying for staff and other store costs. China’s licensing change can improve the consolidated margin mechanically, so North American margin progress matters more.
